The seventh floor of corporate headquarters smelled of industrial carpet cleaner, stale roast coffee, and impending dread. Above the endless sea of gray felt cubicles, the fluorescent lighting hummed at a specific, maddening frequency designed to erode morale. It had started with a calendar invite. Sent at 4:58 PM on a Friday with no attached agenda, the cryptic placeholder titled *Operational Alignment & Optimization Update* had instantly sent shockwaves through the department. Rumors swirled faster than the sputtering fan in the executive washroom. External management consultants had reportedly been spotted in the lower lobby, brandishing sleek aluminum clipboards, color-coded spreadsheets, and the terrifyingly polite smiles of professionals tasked with trimming departmental fat. 

For the moment, keycards still beeped green at the security turnstiles, and the breakroom water cooler maintained its gentle, oblivious bubble. The company Slack channels remained eerily quiet, save for a few nervous thumbs-up reactions to an automated birthday announcement. Yet the tension was palpable across every ergonomic task chair. Restructuring was imminent, the budget was bleeding, and someone was bound to leave with their worldly belongings stuffed into a single cardboard box.
